varsom.explanation: "Varsom" means "cautious". To say what you are careful with, add "med" (with): "at være varsom med sine ord" (to choose your words with care).

vaskepulver.explanation: "Vaskepulver" means "laundry detergent". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "et pulver" (a powder). The word for any kind of detergent, powder or liquid, is "et vaskemiddel" (a detergent): "Vaskemidlet står på hylden" (The detergent is on the shelf).

vasketøj.explanation: "Vasketøj" means "laundry". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "tøj" (clothes). To say you have a lot of laundry, use no article before "vasketøj": "Jeg har meget vasketøj" (I have a lot of laundry).

ved.explanation: "Ved" means "by". To say where someone sits next to something: "Han sidder ved vinduet" (He sits by the window). When you talk about a table or desk where someone sits or works, it means "at": "Vi sidder ved bordet" (We sit at the table). The same spelling is also a form of "at vide" (to know): "Jeg ved det" (I know it).

ved siden af.explanation: "Ved siden af" means "next to". It is built from "ved" (by), "siden" (the side) and "af" (of), so literally by the side of. To say you do something in addition to a job: "Jeg læser ved siden af mit arbejde" (I study alongside my job).

vedholdenhed.explanation: "En vedholdenhed" means "a persistence". To say that a task needs it: "Det kræver vedholdenhed at skrive en bog" (It takes persistence to write a book). For the strength of your body, use "udholdenhed" (stamina): "Maratonløbere har stor udholdenhed" (Marathon runners have great stamina).

vedkommende.explanation: "Vedkommende" means "the person". To talk about a person without saying "han" (he) or "hun" (she): "Vedkommende har ikke svaret" (The person has not answered).

vedligeholdelse.explanation: "Vedligeholdelse" means "maintenance". To talk about fixing something that is already broken, use "en reparation" (a repair): "Bilen skal til reparation" (The car needs repair).

vedrørende.explanation: "Vedrørende" means "regarding". To name the subject of a letter or email, write it first: "Vedrørende din bestilling" (Regarding your order). It is shortened to "vedr." in writing.

vedvarende.explanation: "Vedvarende" means "persistent". It comes from "at vare" (to last). In "vedvarende energi" it means "renewable".

vedvarende energi.explanation: "Vedvarende energi" means "renewable energy". It is "vedvarende" (lasting) and "energi" (energy), so literally lasting energy.

vegansk.explanation: "Vegansk" means "vegan". To talk about a person who eats this way, use "en veganer" (a vegan): "Min søster er veganer" (My sister is a vegan).

vegetarisk.explanation: "Vegetarisk" means "vegetarian". To ask a restaurant for food without meat: "Har I noget vegetarisk?" (Do you have anything vegetarian?) To talk about a person who eats this way, use "en vegetar" (a vegetarian): "Min bror er vegetar" (My brother is a vegetarian).

vejarbejde.explanation: "Vejarbejde" means "roadworks". It is built from "en vej" (a road) and "et arbejde" (a job). To warn about a road: "Der er vejarbejde på motorvejen" (There are roadworks on the highway).

vejr.explanation: "Vejr" means "weather". To ask what it is like outside: "Hvordan er vejret?" (How is the weather?) The same word is also in "at trække vejret" (to breathe), where it means "the breath": "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe).

vejrtrækning.explanation: "En vejrtrækning" means "a breath / breathing". It is built on "at trække vejret" (to take a breath), where "vejret" means "the breath" here, not the weather. To say you hold your breath: "Jeg holder vejret" (I am holding my breath).

vel.explanation: "Vel" means "I suppose". To say you guess that something is fine: "Det er vel i orden" (I suppose that is fine). To ask a question where you expect the answer no: "Han er vel ikke gået?" (He has not left, has he?)

velbegrundet.explanation: "Velbegrundet" means "well-founded". It is built from "vel" (well) and "begrundet" (given reasons for).

velbekomme.explanation: "Velbekomme" means "Enjoy! / You're welcome!". When you put food in front of someone, say it: "Velbekomme!" (Enjoy!) When someone thanks you for a meal, say it back: "Tak for en dejlig middag." "Velbekomme." (Thanks for a lovely dinner. You're welcome.) For other thanks, say "selv tak" (you're welcome): "Tak for hjælpen." "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. You're welcome.)

veldrevet.explanation: "Veldrevet" means "well-run". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at drive" (to run), as in "en veldrevet butik" (a well-run shop). For a place that looks neat and cared for, use "velholdt" (well-kept): "et velholdt hus" (a well-kept house).

velfortjent.explanation: "Velfortjent" means "well-deserved". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at fortjene" (to deserve). The opposite is "ufortjent" (undeserved): "Det var en ufortjent sejr" (It was an undeserved win).

velfærd.explanation: "Velfærd" means "welfare". In Denmark it especially means public services paid for by taxes, such as health care, schools and care for the old. A country that provides them is "en velfærdsstat" (a welfare state): "Danmark er en velfærdsstat" (Denmark is a welfare state).

velfærdssamfundet.explanation: "Et velfærdssamfund" means "a welfare society". It is built from "velfærd" (welfare) and "et samfund" (a society). In Denmark, taxes pay for things such as schools and health care.

velgørenhed.explanation: "Velgørenhed" means "charity". For a charity as an organization, use "en velgørenhedsorganisation" (a charity organization): "Jeg giver penge til en velgørenhedsorganisation" (I give money to a charity organization).

velhavende.explanation: "Velhavende" means "wealthy". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at have" (to have). A shorter word with the same meaning is "rig" (rich): "Han er rig" (He is rich).
